candidates.title: Compare chained agent answers for added claims

demandEvidence.chore: Review whether successive language-model answers introduce unsupported additions or missed edge cases.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: How does this not end up in a chinese whisper game, especially considering how much LLMs infer, guess, and find edge cases and whatnot everywhere?

experimentPlan.output: A side-by-side review sheet that marks claims added or changed between two supplied agent answers for a human to inspect.
experimentPlan.trigger: A professional operator has two sequential model answers that need a consistency review.
steps: Paste the original question and both answers into a local test form.
Split each answer into short factual claims.
Compare claim wording and mark possible additions or omissions.
Show matched text and uncertain pairs in a review sheet.
Have a person verify every flag against trusted reference facts.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On fictional answer pairs, check whether the sheet shows each deliberately added claim and does not label the proposed flags as verified falsehoods.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies the text and trusted facts, decides whether a difference is actually wrong, and does not rely on the tool as a truth verifier.
unverified: No implementation reference supports claim extraction or comparison.
Whether a useful comparison can distinguish paraphrase from changed meaning is unresolved.
The post states a concern but does not establish repeated frequency or a paying buyer.

ease.reason: A supplied-text mock is definable, but no implementation reference supports claim extraction or comparison.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: teams using chained models may pay for review; this question establishes no buyer intent.

feasibility.reason: A fictional pair comparison is bounded, but defining useful flags and avoiding false claims remains unresolved.

autonomy.reason: Text comparison could repeat, but a person must verify truth and judge each flagged difference.

evidence.reason: The question states concern about inference and edge cases, without examples, frequency, or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: a comparison mock can be scoped to the stated concern, but truth assessment, repeated need, and buyer demand are unsupported.

candidates.title: Draft a follow-up for a delayed app review

demandEvidence.chore: Prepare a polite status inquiry for an app submission whose review has remained pending.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Could you please share an estimated timeline, or let us know if anything is needed from our side?

experimentPlan.output: A draft status inquiry based only on an operator-entered submission date and current review status.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator notices that a submitted app remains in the same review status and wants to prepare a follow-up.
steps: Enter the submission date and review status manually.
Generate a neutral summary of elapsed time without claiming a cause.
Draft a concise request for an estimated timeline or missing information.
Show the source fields beside the draft for review.
Have the operator edit and send it through the approved channel.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For fictional submission dates and statuses, verify that the draft repeats only entered facts and asks for an update without inventing a reason for delay.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person checks the current portal status, chooses whether and when to contact the platform, verifies the recipient, and sends the message.
unverified: No reference supports reading app-review status or portal data.
No evidence shows this task recurs across a buyer group.
The supplied post reports one case and does not establish willingness to pay.

ease.reason: An operator can supply dates and review status for a draft, but no reference supports portal access.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: independent app developers may value follow-up help; one case does not establish a paying market.

feasibility.reason: A manually supplied status-to-draft mock is bounded, while useful timing and recurrence remain unknown.

autonomy.reason: It can draft from entered facts, but a person must verify status, choose contact, and send.

evidence.reason: The retained context reports a 55-day pending review and asks for a timeline, but gives no recurrence or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: a follow-up draft is possible from manual inputs, but this is one platform-specific case with no repeated need or buyer evidence.

candidates.title: Check weekly keyword rows before reporting

demandEvidence.chore: Collect weekly keyword volume, CPC, and difficulty values and add them as rows in Google Sheets.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: adds each keyword’s Google search volume, CPC and difficulty as rows in Google Sheets.

experimentPlan.output: A review table that checks operator-supplied keyword metric rows for missing values and highlights them before spreadsheet entry.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator has a weekly batch of keyword metrics and wants to review row completeness before adding them to a sheet.
steps: Paste fictional keyword metric rows into a local form.
Check that each row has the three expected metric fields.
Flag blank or malformed values without filling them in.
Display a review table grouped by keyword.
Have a person verify values and add approved rows to their own sheet.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: With fictional rows containing known blanks and malformed values, verify that only those rows are flagged and no metric is guessed or altered.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person obtains and verifies metrics, supplies them, decides how to resolve flags, and controls any Google Sheets entry.
unverified: The described maker workflow is not independent evidence of customer demand.
No supplied reference supports metric retrieval or Google Sheets writing.
Actual data formats and metric validation rules are not documented.

ease.reason: A row completeness mock is approachable, but no reference supports retrieving metrics or writing Sheets rows.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: marketing consultants may value weekly reporting, but this maker workflow establishes no buyer intent.

feasibility.reason: Synthetic row checks are bounded; accurate retrieval, validation rules, and sheet access remain unsupported.

autonomy.reason: Completeness checks repeat on supplied rows, but a person must obtain metrics and approve sheet changes.

evidence.reason: The context describes weekly metric fields and spreadsheet rows in one maker workflow, not independent customer demand.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: concrete fields support a synthetic completeness check, but the source is a maker workflow and implementation support or buyer demand is absent.

candidates.title: Review which site pages still serve a purpose

demandEvidence.chore: Review whether an existing site page answers a question or solves a problem before keeping it.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Before adding anything new I check whether the page already has a reason to exist.

experimentPlan.output: A review worksheet that flags supplied page descriptions with no stated purpose for a person to inspect.
experimentPlan.trigger: A site editor is reviewing a supplied list of existing or proposed pages.
steps: Paste fictional page descriptions and purpose statements.
Check whether each purpose field is blank.
Summarize the stated purpose without asserting page quality.
Flag blank or unclear entries for editorial review.
Have a person decide whether to keep, change, or remove a page.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Using fictional page records with known blank purpose fields, confirm those rows are flagged and populated pages are not automatically judged unnecessary.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies context and decides the page's value; the worksheet cannot determine audience needs or delete pages.
unverified: The source is a personal tip and does not establish a repeated customer burden.
No implementation reference supports page inventory or purpose classification.
No buyer or payment evidence is supplied.

ease.reason: A supplied-text worksheet is possible, but reliable page-purpose classification is undocumented.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small web studios may pay for content review; this tip establishes no buyer intent.

feasibility.reason: A fictional list review is bounded, though judging actual audience value needs human context.

autonomy.reason: A form can flag missing purpose statements, but a person must judge and change each page.

evidence.reason: The excerpt gives a keep-or-delete heuristic, but no specific repeated need or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: the stated review rule can be mocked, but the post is a personal tip without evidence of recurring customer demand.

candidates.title: Draft shipment delay notices from sample rows

demandEvidence.chore: Notify a dispatcher when a shipment is delayed.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: A simple flow can notify a dispatcher when a shipment is delayed

experimentPlan.output: A draft delay notice and exception row based on an operator-supplied fictional shipment status.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies a shipment row marked delayed under their own stated rule.
steps: Enter fictional shipment status and the operator's delay rule.
Compare the supplied status with that rule.
Draft a short notice using only entered fields.
Show the triggering fields beside the draft.
Have a dispatcher verify the status and approve any real notice.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For fictional rows with pre-labeled delay conditions, confirm that only matching rows produce drafts and that no external status is inferred.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies accurate status and rules, verifies the exception, and authorizes any notice; live carrier and CRM connections are excluded.
unverified: The source gives this as an example, not evidence of an actual operator request or recurrence.
No supplied reference supports logistics event intake or message delivery.
Useful delay rules and the buyer's workflow are unspecified.

ease.reason: A sample-row draft is straightforward to outline, but no reference supports logistics intake or delivery.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small logistics operators may pay for clearer notices; this article example establishes no buying intent.

feasibility.reason: A fictional row-to-draft experiment is bounded, while real event access and correct delay rules remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: Drafting can repeat on supplied rows, but a person must verify status and approve messages.

evidence.reason: The article names a dispatcher alert among examples, without a direct request, frequency, or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: an example supports a narrow synthetic test, but the article does not establish an actual repeated customer chore or implementation capability.
